incident-bot: PAGERDUTY alert opened (sev 2) — us-west-2a: sustained egress path slowdown detected on inference fleet (latency spike + sporadic 502s). Auto-escalation to oncall.sre.
Monica S: Seeing p95 token latency jump from ~120ms -> 420ms across the shard pool. Error rate up ~4% -> 9%. Dashboards: https://dash.redwood/boards/ingest/az1a-egress
Kai L: traces show long socket send queues on several nodes, rx_queue/backlog growth on eth0 counters. Running quick check on node g5-az1a-78:```sudo ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx_queue|tx_queue|tx_busy"```returns large rx_queue_drops and tx_busy. Also `netstat -anp | grep FIN` shows lots of half-closed connections.
Raj P: Are we sure this is local AZ network plane and not NAT throttling? I see NAT gateway metrics in the VPC console spiking on retries.
Monica S: NAT metrics are normal-ish, but ENI RX drops and instance-level kernel queue lengths are high. Could be hypervisor host network saturation or driver regression.
Kai L: Short-term mitigation: route inference traffic for critical customers to other healthy AZs / fallback region and reduce per-request tokens (prompt truncation) for non-critical traffic. I'm going to trigger smart-routing fallback for model family redwood-large -> redwood-large-quantized-small in us-west-2b.
Monica S: Adding runbook step — deregister unhealthy targets from NLB (so we stop filling queues) and spin up replacement instances in other AZs. Use these commands:```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --targets Id=i-0abc1234```and for quick spin:```asg-cli scale --asg inference-usw2a --to 6```
Ingrid T: I'll take traffic steering and customer comms. Monica, can you confirm which customers are above the impact threshold?
Monica S: Looking now: approx 8% of requests in us-west-2a failing or timing out; customers with reserved capacity unaffected. A handful of high-throughput hosted API keys (~3) see degraded latency >1s. We'll flag them for support.
support-bot: Notifying customers tagged "platform-critical" in us-west-2a with templated message.
Raj P: Can we flip DNS resolver fallback sooner? I see resolver latencies increase to 200-300ms causing extra SLO chattiness. Maybe we should force resolver to internal-cached endpoint.
Kai L: I'm going to temporarily pin service discovery to internal resolver IP on affected nodes: edit /etc/resolv.conf -> prepend 10.0.2.5 (internal cache) and restart dnsmasq on instances. Doing now on a small batch for canary.
deploy-bot: Canary update applied to 3 instances in asg inference-usw2a at 2217765467.
Monica S: Canary is green for those nodes — rx_queue usage dropped after restarting dnsmasq and pre-pinning resolver. However other nodes still show kernel-level tx/rx wait.
Raj P: Possible NIC firmware or hypervisor IO congestion. I've opened a ticket with cloud provider support (case 987654321). ETA unknown.
Ingrid T: Handing paging & coordination to Kai for next 2h window — I'm going to coordinate customer outreach and post-incident comms. Kai, please own live mitigation and hand off to next oncall if you need break. @kai
Kai L: Ack, taking lead. Current mitigation plan: 1) deregister worst-off targets from NLB, 2) enable cross-AZ routing for critical routes, 3) fallback to quantized model variants for non-critical traffic, 4) pin resolver and restart dns cache on remaining nodes, 5) monitor error rate and token latency.
Monica S: Quick status update after first steps: deregistered 12 targets, spun new instances in us-west-2b, smart-routing moved ~22% of requests successfully. Error rate dropped from 9% -> 3.1% in 18 minutes.
support-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2026-112 for affected customers, escalation level: engineering + account execs.
Raj P: Cloud support responded: they see host-level transmit queue backlog on several hypervisors in us-west-2a and are investigating noisy neighbor. Recommended live-migration of impacted instances.
Kai L: We're scheduling live-migrations for the top 8 nodes after draining. Commands I'm using to drain and live-migrate:```kubectl cordon node/node-az1a-xx && kubectl drain node/node-az1a-xx --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```followed by cloud CLI to request host move.
Monica S: After first two live-migrations, node metrics improved (rx drops -> near 0). Continuing migration for remaining nodes.
Ingrid T: Customer impact summary for comms: brief latency increase for ~8% of hosted API traffic in us-west-2a between 2217765432-2217765600. Most customers auto-failed over; 3 high-throughput keys saw >1s latency and increased 502s briefly. No data loss.
Kai L: Paging handoff: I'll be on this for the next 90 minutes, then hand to Ingrid for follow-up/root-cause. If cloud support confirms hypervisor noisy neighbor we likely need a postmortem and mitigation triage (nic firmware pinned, cross-az capacity buffer).
Monica S: Adding postmortem owner tag: Ingrid T. Action items: 1) cloud support escalation until resolution, 2) add auto-migration rule when rx_drop > X, 3) tune resolver timeout/pinning for future, 4) run a capacity test for AZ failure.
Ingrid T: Copy. I'll own the postmortem and customer comms. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Pagerduty incident #2342 set to status: acknowledged. Last update 2217765699
